display.purpose: The arched 'RESUME / ROAST' masthead lettering (46px for ROAST), SVG textPath, red with a 6px ink stroke under the fill and a 3px ink drop shade. Masthead and share card only.

score.purpose: The count-up score on the burst, red with a 2px ink text stroke, tabular figures; the /10 at 22px.

numeral.purpose: Fix numbers in red circles (yellow); the heat count line at 19px in red.

seal.purpose: Words inside starbursts: the heat badge and the OR divider, in Pale Butter.

headline.purpose: One screen title per screen, between two red stars; 27px under 360px.

title.purpose: Route card titles; 25px sheet title, 21px drop zone title.

button.purpose: Every button label; 23px on big buttons, 19-20px in two-up rows and provider chips.

narrative.overview:
The whole app is one hot sauce bottle label. A label-red ground runs the full height of the phone; an arched butter-yellow banner with halftone dots carries fat outlined lettering flanked by two glossy chillies; a cream paper panel hangs under it with a starburst heat badge pinned across its top edge and a row of flame tongues burning along its bottom edge. Every screen is a different panel on the same label: the route cards, the heat picker, the stamped roast lines, the score burst and the three fixes. The share card is the same label redrawn on a 1080 x 1920 canvas with the same palette object and the same banner, seal, burst, star and flame paths.

The material is printed paper and ink. Depth comes from 2.5px ink outlines and inset double keylines, not from shadows; colour comes from two sauces, red and yellow, on warm cream, with brown-black ink instead of grey. Things that are a verdict (the heat, the score, each roast line) sit on starbursts and seals and arrive with a stamp; things you operate (route cards, fields, buttons) stay square, outlined and still. Density is phone-first and generous: one 460px column, 44px minimum targets, one screen title per screen.

The category look this rejects is the grey "AI resume analyser" dashboard with a score ring. The label is cheeky and loud, but every sentence is set in a readable slab serif at 13.5px or larger, and red text below 18px moves to the deeper red so it stays legible on cream.
keyCharacteristics: Label red frame, butter-yellow banner, cream paper panel, flame-tongue bottom edge.
Ink outlines on everything: 2.5px on cards, buttons, fields and chips; 3px on the panel, sheet and desktop bottle.
Three typefaces with fixed jobs: Ultra lettering, Barlow Condensed label caps and titles, Zilla Slab sentences.
Starbursts and seals carry heat, score and roast lines; numbered circles carry the fixes.
Results stamp in; controls press down 1-2px; reduced motion removes all of it.
Warm neutrals only: no grey, no blue.

rules.name: The Two Sauces Rule
rules.body: Red and yellow are the only colours with jobs. Green is limited to stems and the "done" state, and the neutrals are warm browns and creams; nothing on the label is grey or blue, and an unlit chilli is desaturated to sepia, not grey.

rules.name: The Small Red Rule
rules.body: Sauce Red text appears only at 18px and up (ruled labels, the heat count, the score). Resting red text below 18px (links, field labels, errors) uses Dried Chilli, which holds 7.4:1 on cream.

rules.name: The Text On Red Rule
rules.body: Text on Sauce Red is Label Cream (4.7:1) or Pale Butter in Ultra (4.5:1). Banner Yellow on red is reserved for the Ultra fix numerals at 21px (3.7:1) and never carries a sentence.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Ultra prints names and numbers, never a sentence. Barlow Condensed prints titles, buttons and caps labels, never a paragraph. Every sentence, including roast lines and the verdict, is Zilla Slab.

rules.name: The Outlined Lettering Rule
rules.body: The masthead lettering and the score are Sauce Red Ultra with an ink outline painted under the fill (paint-order: stroke). Ultra used for seal words, fix numerals and the heat count is flat: Pale Butter or Banner Yellow on a red seal, or Sauce Red on cream.

rules.name: The One Bottle Rule
rules.body: Everything lives in the 460px label column. Wider screens get the butter backdrop around the bottle, never a wider bottle or a second column.

rules.name: The Ink Line Rule
rules.body: Every card, button, field, chip, seal and frame carries an ink outline: 2.5px on components (the `--line` value), 3px on the panel, sheet and desktop bottle, 2px on textareas, the file chip and the error line. A surface without an outline is not part of the label.

rules.name: The Double Keyline Rule
rules.body: Containers that mark a moment (the panel, the cooking card, the error card, the back button) get an inset double keyline; ordinary cards do not.

rules.name: The Starburst Rule
rules.body: Heat, score and roast lines sit on seals and bursts; ordered fixes sit in plain red circles. A seal never wraps a control.

rules.name: The Hand-Placed Tilt Rule
rules.body: Stamped and illustrated things are slightly off-square: roast quote cards alternate -0.7deg and 0.6deg, their seals turn 14deg or -10deg, picker chillies tilt -6deg and 5deg, the score chillies lean at 62deg. Route cards, fix cards, fields and buttons stay square.

dos: Do outline every card, button, field, chip and seal in Smoked Ink (#2A120B): 2.5px on components, 3px on the panel, the sheet and the desktop bottle.
Do keep sentences in Zilla Slab at 13.5px or larger, in Smoked Ink or Tamarind on cream surfaces.
Do put text on Sauce Red in Label Cream (4.7:1) or, in Ultra, Pale Butter; use Dried Chilli (#9E1410) for any red text under 18px.
Do put heat, score and roast lines on seals and bursts, and let results stamp in with the shared ease-out curve.
Do use dashed ink borders only for places that receive something: the drop zone, the heat readout, the prompt preview.
Do mark example content with the ink ribbon ("Example: a made-up resume") on screen and on the share card.
Do keep every tap target at 44px or more and keep the 3px ink outline plus 7px yellow halo for keyboard focus.
Do redraw the share card from the same palette, fonts and SVG paths as the page.
donts: Don't use grey or blue anywhere on the label; neutrals are warm browns and creams, and an unlit chilli goes sepia.
Don't cast shadows from cards, buttons or chips; depth is the ink outline and the inset double keyline. The bottle float on wide screens is the only cast shadow.
Don't set a sentence in Ultra or Barlow Condensed, or a name or number meant to shout in Zilla Slab.
Don't set the masthead lettering or the score as flat red Ultra without its ink outline.
Don't show provider logos; providers are plain names on chips.
Don't widen the 460px label column or add a second column on large screens.
Don't tilt or stamp controls; tilt and stamps belong to results and illustrations.
Don't use Banner Yellow text on red for anything but the 21px Ultra fix numerals.
